question: Should the bundled Policy plugin permanently own declarative routing-conformance probes and their scoped-overlay/attestation contract, or should this remain an external/operator workflow?
rationale: This is a new persisted Policy capability, not a repair of an established contract; code review can assess implementation quality but cannot choose whether this grammar and its long-term compatibility burden belong in the bundled plugin.

options.title: Sponsor the Policy contract
options.body: Approve the opt-in routing section as a bundled Policy capability, contingent on documented semantics and redacted real-run proof before merge.

options.title: Keep it external
options.body: Decline the bundled grammar and direct operators to an external policy or monitoring workflow if this is not a core Policy responsibility.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the Policy contract
recommendation.body: Approve the opt-in routing section as a bundled Policy capability, contingent on documented semantics and redacted real-run proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Current-main ownership could not be established from the supplied review material, so a Policy-area maintainer should make the product decision rather than the contributor alone.
